## CPython 3.13 Free Threading and Extension Support

CPython 3.13 introduced experimental free threading as a configuration that can run with the Global Interpreter Lock (GIL) disabled. In this mode, an application’s runtime choice is connected to the extensions it imports: importing an extension without an explicit free-threading support declaration triggers a warning and enables the GIL.

The declaration mechanism depends on how the extension is initialized. Multi-phase and single-phase initialization use different mechanisms, but in either case the declaration communicates compatibility with the free-threaded mode.

For extension authors, declaring compatibility is separate from making the extension’s code thread-safe. A support declaration does not itself make the code thread-safe or establish that it is.
